newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise in May.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise in May.

text.p: Lebanese government revenues from taxation of property deals rose 13.15 percent in May over the same month last year, according to figures released by the finance ministry on Monday.
The ministry collected $14,128,131 compared with $12,485,683 in May 1996. It collected $10,134,274 in April.
Collected property tax revenues for the first five months of 1997 totalled $56,860,300 compared with $49,136,825 over the same period a year earlier -- a rise of 15.72 percent.
Tax rates on property deals vary from district to district, but average about 6.5 percent.
However, tax collection does not truly reflect the state of the market because deals are sometimes understated to avoid tax, property analysts say.
